figures.finding: Chargeable income is taxed at 25% up to TTD 1 million and 30% above, after a personal allowance of TTD 90,000 for every resident.

sources.said: The income tax rate for individuals with chargeable income less than TTD 1 million is 25%. For chargeable income in excess of TTD 1 million, the rate of tax applicable is 30%.
The Personal Allowance - $90,000 as of 01/01/2023

figures.finding: A self-employed person with receipts over TTD 360,000 a year pays business levy of 0.6% of gross receipts where it exceeds the income tax (not in the first three years).

sources.said: Business levy of 0.6% is applicable to sole traders and self-employed individuals having gross income or receipts in excess of TTD 360,000 per annum .

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; a return is due by 30 April of the next year (residents with only employment income need not file), and any shortfall is paid by the same date.

sources.said: The tax year corresponds to the calendar year in Trinidad and Tobago. Tax returns Tax returns must be filed by 30 April of the year following the calendar or accounting year-end.
Resident individuals earning only employment income are not required to file a tax return.

figures.finding: Tax is withheld from emoluments under PAYE, using the employee's TD1 form; deductions are remitted by the 15th of the next month.

sources.said: It is the system by which tax is withheld from emolument Income (The PAYE System). Therefore it is necessary for the employee to submit a TD 1 Form to the employer.
Deductions made in January must be remitted by the 15th February

figures.finding: A foreign artiste's fee, paid by a promoter to a non-resident not engaged in trade or business in Trinidad and Tobago, bears 15% withholding tax on the gross payment (fees and charges for personal services), remitted within thirty days; the withholding replaces income tax on that payment, so it is final, and a treaty may lower it.
figures.applies: Non-resident individuals not engaged in trade or business in Trinidad and Tobago (Income Tax Act ss. 50, 51 and Third Schedule Part II, as revised to 31 December 2016; later amendments to the rate were not seen).

figures.finding: National Insurance is 16.2% from January 2026, up to TTD 508.50 a week (TTD 339.00 employer, 169.50 employee) at monthly income of TTD 13,600 or more, rising to 19.2% in January 2027; a health surcharge of up to TTD 8.25 a week is also withheld.

sources.said: Effective January 2026, the contribution rate is 16.2%. The maximum total weekly contribution is TTD 508.50 for monthly income of TTD 13,600 and over, payable as TTD 339.00 by the employer and TTD 169.50 by the employee. Effective January 2027, the contribution rate increases to 19.2%.
The maximum rate is TTD 8.25 per week for monthly income over TTD 470.

figures.finding: A fee bears 12.5% VAT once gross receipts reach TTD 600,000 in 12 months (artistes' promoters and bandleaders included).

sources.said: The standard rate applicable to commercial supplies is 12.5%.
PROMOTERS ARE TO BE REGISTERED FOR VAT where gross receipts of six hundred thousand dollars ($600 000) is attained (as of 1/1/2023)
